english.title: Possess a dead / part of a dead badger
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), had in your possession or under your control

(A)_[a dead badger]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY NUMBER..) dead badgers]_
(C)_[part of or anything derived from a dead badger]_
(D)_[parts of or anything derived from a dead badger]_
(E)_[parts of or anything derived from dead badgers]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(3) and 12 of the Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also general exceptions to badger offences, exceptions to section 1 offences, and exemption licences.
(ii) If more than one badger was involved, the fine shall be determined as if there were separate offences for each one.
(iii) See also power of forfeiture under subsection 12(4) of the Act.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions: Complex, see section 12ZA.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
